title: Missing error handling for non-OK HTTP responses in chat API call
reasoning: The code calls fetch and immediately tries to parse JSON without checking res.ok or res.status. If the server returns a 4xx or 5xx status, res.json() may succeed (if the server sent JSON error body) or fail (if it sent HTML or plain text). A 500 error page or a network-level non-JSON response will cause res.json() to throw, hitting the catch block with a generic 'Error connecting to Kit' message. This hides the actual HTTP error (e.g. 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 500 Internal Server Error) from the user and makes debugging harder.
reproduction:
1. Modify backend /api/kit-chat to return 500 with plain text 'Internal Server Error'
2. Send a message
3. Observe generic 'Error connecting to Kit' instead of a more specific error message
recommendation: Check res.ok before parsing JSON. If !res.ok, read res.status and res.statusText and display a more informative error (e.g. 'Server error (500)', 'Unauthorized (401)'). If the response is JSON, parse and show data.error; otherwise show status text.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are provided. A test that mocks fetch to return non-200 status would catch this.
suggestedRegressionTest: Mock fetch to return 500 with non-JSON body and verify the UI displays a helpful error message, not just 'Error connecting to Kit'.
